pipeline.name: Team Collaboration Brief
pipeline.description: Turn a free-form problem statement into a hand-off brief for a teammate: scope, acceptance criteria, suggested approach, and a draft GitHub issue. Demonstrates the v0.3 multi-user import flow — the importer becomes the owner, no user_id is embedded in this bundle.

tpl_team_scope.name: Scope Extractor
tpl_team_scope.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <task>
    Read the problem statement in <description> and extract a
    structured outline. Emit ONE markdown block of the shape:

    ## title
    (a ~50-char summary suitable as a GitHub issue title)

    ## scope
    (1-2 sentences naming what is in/out)

    ## constraints
    (any obvious must-haves, one per line; or "none" if none)

    Write the entire markdown block into ``implementation_notes``
    in the <output> block — downstream nodes append to the same
    field.
  </task>
  <description>{{ description }}</description>
  <constraints>
    If <description> is empty, write
    ``## title\n(empty)\n## scope\n(no actionable scope)`` so
    downstream nodes still have a valid shape to consume.
  </constraints>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_team_brief.name: Brief Drafter
tpl_team_brief.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <task>
    The current <implementation_notes> contains the structured
    outline from the previous node (title / scope / constraints).
    Append three more sections to it:

    ## acceptance criteria
    (a 3-5 bullet ``- [ ]`` checklist of done conditions)

    ## suggested approach
    (2-4 sentences naming the implementation path)

    ## risks
    (1-3 things the teammate should verify before merging)

    Write the FULL updated markdown (original outline + the three
    new sections, in that order) into ``implementation_notes``.
    Be concrete but don't over-prescribe — the teammate is the
    one doing the work.
  </task>
  <implementation_notes>{{ implementation_notes }}</implementation_notes>
</agent_prompt>

tpl_team_issue.name: GitHub Issue Formatter
tpl_team_issue.prompt_template:
<agent_prompt version="1">
  <role>{{ role }}</role>
  <task>
    The current <implementation_notes> contains the full brief
    in markdown. Rewrite it into a GitHub-issue-friendly body:

    - Strip the ``## title`` section (it goes in the issue title,
      not the body) but copy its content into a new top-level H1.
    - Keep the other sections, normalised to ``## Context`` /
      ``## Acceptance criteria`` / ``## Suggested approach`` /
      ``## Risks``.
    - Ensure every acceptance-criteria bullet starts with
      ``- [ ]`` so GitHub renders it as a task list.
    - End with a single line:
      ``> Generated by the team-collaboration pipeline``

    Write the final markdown into ``implementation_notes``. The
    operator pipes it next via:
      ``gh issue create --title "<H1 line>" --body-file <(...)``
  </task>
  <implementation_notes>{{ implementation_notes }}</implementation_notes>
</agent_prompt>
